articles.title: Ukraine accuses Russia of targeting rescue operation after 'double-tap' strike kills 72
articles.summary: Efforts to recover bodies after a “double-tap” attack in southern Ukraine are being hampered by continuing Russian strikes, officials say.
articles.body: Ukraine accuses Russia of targeting rescuers after ‘double-tap’ strike Ukrainian officials have accused Russia of targeting rescue and recovery operations two weeks after a deadly "double-tap" strike at a village close to the front line killed at least 72 people. Ukraine says Russia carried out two attacks in succession on a humanitarian aid centre in the village of Komyshuvakha on 2 November - including the use of what it said was a 3,000kg (6,600lb) aerial bomb on a shelter where residents had fled for safety. Verified images posted in the days after the attack show damage to emergency vehicles and excavation equipment at the site. The State Emergency Service of Ukraine (DSNS) told BBC Verify there were multiple Russian strikes during the rescue. The DSNS said three police officers, four workers and two rescue dogs were injured while five vehicles were damaged during the operation, which has now concluded. With the DSNS saying the death toll had risen to at least 72 people, the attack on Komyshuvakha has become the second deadliest single incident of the Ukraine war. Oleksiy, an intelligence officer investigating the incident for Ukraine's SBU security service, who asked to be identified only by his first name, said rescue vehicles were "clearly marked" and accused Russia of "deliberately destroying humanitarian equipment". He added the village's infrastructure and the people still living in Komyshuvakha are also being systematically targeted by drones and bombs. Oleksiy accused Russian forces of "outright terror against civilians, against peaceful residents" to make life on the front line impossible. BBC Verify has confirmed videos being shared by Ukrainian police that show rescue workers at the scene shouting "drone, drone" and running for cover on the day after the 2 November attack. A group can also be seen treating a victim. Oleksiy said rescue crews operated under a constant threat of attack. "The enemy knows perfectly well that what is being carried out there is essentially a humanitarian operation to search for the dead," he said. BBC Verify has asked the Russian Ministry of Defence for comment specifically about the Komyshuvakha attacks but has not received a response. A general statement released on 2 November by the Russian MoD said it had targeted energy and transport infrastructure used by the Ukrainian military across the country. While there are no military or industrial facilities in Komyshuvakha it is close to a key route used for Ukrainian troop movements, supplies and evacuations. The village was previously reported to have been struck by the Russians on 28 October. Local people headed to the shelter area on 2 November after being told by a local Telegram group that aid would be distributed between 10:00 and 12:00 local time (08:00-10:00 GMT). Ukrainian authorities said an initial strike, at 09:45 local time, hit buildings above ground killing one woman. Video shows moments between deadly Russian attacks on village in Ukraine Bodycam footage, released by Ukrainian police in edited segments and analysed by BBC Verify, shows people trying to free a casualty from the rubble before declaring she had died. Throughout the footage, warnings of an impending second strike can be heard on police radios with increasing urgency until people are instructed to run to the underground shelter. The same footage, which was taken around an hour after the first attack, goes on to show people in a shelter. As they wait in silence a large explosion can be heard and the video goes dark. Aftermath video filmed later shows bodies being recovered from a large crater immediately above the shelter. Twisted iron and rubble from the structure below can be seen beneath the surface. Funerals have been held almost daily for the victims of the attack, including locals working to administer aid distribution, those seeking to collect it and soldiers who officials say arrived to assist with rescue efforts. Trevor Ball, bomb disposal expert at intelligence firm at Armament Research Services, said a crater seen in the footage was consistent with the damage and depth left by a FAB-3000, a 3,000kg Russian bomb which can destroy underground structures. His comments were echoed by Chris Proops, an ex-UK National Crime Agency investigator, who said the scale of the damage at the scene matched the size of the FAB-3000. Ball and Proops both confirmed verified photos of munition fragments obtained by BBC Verify from Ukrainian authorities show part of a guidance kit that is compatible with the FAB-3000, which increases the weapon's accuracy and allows it to be fired from a greater distance from the target. International law experts told BBC Verify that Russia had committed a war crime if it knowingly attacked rescue workers. Ben Saul, professor of international law at the University of Sydney, said this "appears to be either a deliberate attack on civilians or civilian objects - a war crime - or an indiscriminate attack - also a war crime". Prof Samuel Moyn of Yale University said "directly targeting rescuers or their equipment is a gross violation of international humanitarian law". Precautions have to be taken to ensure that strikes target combatants rather than others, he added.

articles.title: US scolds Ukraine over deep strikes ahead of fresh Russia peace talks
articles.summary: German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius slammed the U.S. criticism as a "stupid thing."
articles.body: German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius slammed the U.S. criticism as a “stupid thing.” BRUSSELS — U.S. deputy Pentagon chief Elbridge Colby on Tuesday hit out at Ukraine for its long-range strike campaign against Russia — a fresh blow to Kyiv as it seeks to shore up its negotiating position during peace talks with Moscow. His comments, made at a meeting primarily aimed at raising further support for Ukraine, come as the U.S. is expected to hold fresh peace negotiations with Ukraine and Russia in the coming weeks. “While the public conversation focuses on the spectacle of deep strikes designed to incur pain on the Russian population, our assessment is that such strikes have not been effective … nor do they contribute to blunting Russia's advances on the front line,” Colby said at a meeting of the Ukrainian Defense Contact Group defense ministers in Brussels. “Such strikes, especially those that target civilian infrastructure ... have actually probably hardened the Russian public's resolve and the Kremlin's own willingness to escalate,” he said, adding: “The balance of advantage in deep strikes may well favor Moscow.” “Criticizing strikes like that in Russia to destroy strategic military … targets is quite a stupid thing,” German Foreign Minister Boris Pistorius said after the meeting. “Instead of criticizing that, we should rather criticize and talk about [Russia’s] terroristic strikes every night.” “It's not for us to tell Ukraine how to fight their war,” U.K. Defence Secretary Wes Streeting told reporters. “In terms of deep strike capability, there's no doubt in my mind that it's helped to degrade [Russian President Vladimir] Putin's war machine.” Ukraine has in recent months stepped up long-range attacks deep inside Russia, targeting depots of the online retailer Wildberries, military facilities, oil refineries and fuel export facilities. It says it has taken out 30% of Russian oil refining capacity. On Tuesday, Ukraine said it had destroyed part of the Kerch bridge linking Russia to Crimea. Washington has long opposed deep strikes against Russia, particularly those that affect oil infrastructure. U.S. President Donald Trump last month accused Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskyy of not wanting to end the war. Zelenskyy has previously said the strikes give Ukraine “equal footing” in negotiations with Russia. Colby urged ministers to keep funding the NATO-backed PURL program, where Ukrainian allies pay for American weapons for Kyiv. “Sustaining the flow of critical munitions is essential for Ukrainian troops to continue holding the front line,” he said. PURL was set up last year after the U.S. stopped directly funding Ukraine's war effort following Trump's return to power. On Tuesday, several countries including Germany, Norway and Sweden announced over $300 million in fresh contributions to the scheme. The U.K. separately announced £240 million in air defense support, including over 1,000 short-range missiles and a dozen air defense radars. NATO allies are still billions short of meeting a €70 billion alliance military aid target for Ukraine this year, and a separate goal of raising at least €12 billion for PURL. NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte told POLITICO he was “cautiously optimistic” allies could still meet the overall target, set at the alliance’s July summit in Ankara. Despite the criticism of long-range strikes, Colby praised Ukraine’s “very effective” use of mid-range strike drones to “deny Russian advances” on the front line. Ukraine last week said it had detected limitations on critical U.S. Starlink satellite services for the second time in two months, a move Kyiv said made it more difficult to intercept Russian drones. Asked about the latest restrictions, Colby demurred, telling reporters: “We are very focused on supporting Ukraine's ability to defend itself and these … mid-range strikes, and we're taking steps that are consistent with that policy.”

articles.title: Ukrainian Defense Minister On Crimea Bridge Strike: 'We're Just Getting Started'
articles.summary: Ukraine has released video of its overnight strikes that damaged the bridge between the mainland and Russian-occupied Crimea, the only direct road and rail link to the peninsula. Asked about the attack, Ukrainian Defense Minister Yevheniy Khmara said "We're just getting started."
articles.body: Ukraine has released video of its overnight strikes that damaged the bridge between the mainland and Russian-occupied Crimea, the only direct road and rail link to the peninsula. Russia launched its own attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure overnight on November 17, damaging two key bridges in Kyiv.

articles.title: Russia’s Lavrov says French troops in Ukraine amount to ‘direct participation’ in war
articles.summary: The Kremlin's foreign minister seized on a French media report to warn Europe against deploying troops to Ukraine.
articles.body: The Kremlin’s foreign minister seized on a French media report to warn Europe against deploying troops to Ukraine. Russia’s top diplomat accused Paris of directly taking part in the Ukraine war following a report that French troops are in the eastern European country carrying out noncombatant operations. “We conveyed our concern through available channels, warning the relevant countries that this is no longer support for Ukraine, but direct participation in the war,” Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov told reporters Tuesday at the East Asia Summit in Manila, adding that French troops were also “assisting in goal setting, providing satellite data and much more.” Lavrov’s comments come a day after Radio France Internationale revealed Paris had kept troops in Ukraine for several months to provide training and equipment maintenance under the “Volia mission.” The troops, who are in the French military detachment in Poland, have been involved in the operation in Ukraine since at least summer 2026, RFI reported. Since the Kremlin launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Russian officials have periodically warned Europe against putting troops into the country, as Moscow looks to deter the continent from participating in Ukraine’s resistance with active soldiers. The Elysée Palace did not immediately respond to POLITICO’s request for comment. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot pledged to fight “tooth and nail” for European security during Monday’s meeting of EU foreign ministers in Brussels, following the announcement that Paris would represent Europe in Ukraine peace talks as part of the “E5,” alongside Germany, Italy, Poland and the U.K. In Manila, Lavrov declined to expand on the upcoming trilateral meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, taking place in Shenzhen in southeastern China on Thursday. “It is broadly clear what the leaders will discuss. They will have an opportunity for a free exchange of views. Be patient. There is very little time left to wait,” Lavrov told reporters.

Rwanda hits back at asylum-seeker return hub criticism
articles.summary: NGOs say Rwanda's human rights record means deportation hub plans fail EU and international law requirements.
articles.body: NGOs say Rwanda’s human rights record means deportation hub plans fail EU and international law requirements. VIENNA — Rwanda’s interior minister has rebuked criticism of a plan by five European Union countries to deport failed asylum-seekers to his country. Austria, Denmark, Germany, Greece and the Netherlands on Monday announced a partnership with Rwanda to set up a deportation hub. They aim to send the first asylum-seekers to the African country in 2027. The plan comes after the EU adopted legislation that allows countries to negotiate deals to build such “return hubs” outside the bloc — as long as they meet human rights standards. The announcement led to a storm of protest from civil society and human rights groups, which said the fundamental rights of people sent to Rwanda cannot be guaranteed. “Human rights in Rwanda are respected and granted to everyone and specifically to refugees who choose to come to our country,” Biruta said Tuesday, speaking on a panel at a conference in Vienna hosted by the International Centre for Migration Policy Development. He argued his country’s migration policies are among the “most progressive” as they allow refugees to work and start a business. In a joint warning against the plan Monday , 47 organizations pointed to a 2023 court decision that slapped down the United Kingdom’s plans to process asylum seekers’ claims in Rwanda. It cited “substantial grounds” to believe that people sent to the African nation would be exposed “to a real risk of ill-treatment by reason of refoulement” — referring to a practice whereby people are forcibly moved to countries where they face real threats. Under a 2013 deal with Israel, people sent to Rwanda “were routinely moved clandestinely to Uganda,” the court added. Biruta said he was “not surprised” by NGOs’ warnings and said the government faced “the same issue” when it was making plans with the U.K. Those plans “didn’t work but … helped to improve our asylum system,” he added. NGOs “always … say that nothing is working, that our human rights record is bad,” Biruta said, “but I’d like them to come forward with an alternative solution.” EU ministers repeatedly stressed Monday that their partnership with Rwanda would meet international and European standards. Biruta said his country would put in place an independent monitoring mechanism and that it wants to involve the International Organization for Migration and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees. Details about such mechanisms and cooperation, as well as how the EU countries and Rwanda will divide responsibilities for the refugees’ wellbeing, have not yet been revealed. “There are still some technical things that have to be solved, including where [the responsibility of ] Europe ends and where Rwanda starts,” Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen told POLITICO after the plan’s announcement. Human rights groups don’t believe the countries can come up with a framework that will guarantee migrants’ rights are respected. Rwanda has an abysmal human rights record, is responsible for serious abuses and war crimes in eastern Congo and engages in transnational repression, Judith Sunderland, senior associate director in the refugee and migrant rights division of Human Rights Watch, told POLITICO. “No amount of nominal safeguards will be sufficient to mitigate the risks of serious human rights violations, particularly as there is unlikely to be any way to implement effective monitoring or seek accountability,” she said. “Given its track record, the fact that Rwanda was even considered, much less chosen, justifies deep skepticism about EU rhetoric about respecting people’s rights.”

articles.title: Trump lands in Asia ahead of talks with Russian and Chinese presidents
articles.summary: The US president said he would be open to a one-on-one meeting with Russia's Vladimir Putin "if it's available".
articles.body: President Trump has arrived in the Philippines' capital on the first leg of a trip to Asia, which will end in a meeting in China with its President Xi Jinping and his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin. A red carpet was rolled out for Trump as he walked off Air Force One in Manila. A band played one of his favourite songs, Y.M.C.A., before he was whisked away by helicopter to a hotel. Trump's first meeting at the Asean Summit was with America's partners in the Quad - India's Narendra Modi, whom he described as a "very tough man", Japan's Sanae Takaichi, who "may be even tougher", and Australia's Anthony Albanese. "Our countries are the four corners of the free, open, stable, prosperous Indo-Pacific," the US president said. "We have outstanding relationships and co-ordinate closely... my phone is always open," Trump added. Many countries in South East Asia have been hit hard by Donald Trump's tariffs and his war on Iran - but their exports to the US rose 30% last year thanks to the AI boom for which the region manufactures many of the components. The US is hoping to draw more countries here into its "Pax Silica" tech and AI ecosystem, and away from China. But China's huge influence in this region cannot easily be challenged, and certainly not in the few hours Trump is in the Philippines. After an overnight stay in Manila, the US president will fly to Shenzhen in China to attend a summit of Asia Pacific leaders and have nuclear talks with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. Asked if he would also be open to a one-on-one meeting with Putin, Trump said: "If it's available, I would". articles.title: Iran dismisses report of alleged 'dirty bomb' attack on Washington
articles.summary: Iran has said CNN's claim that Tehran would attack Washington with a "dirty bomb" was an attempt to manufacture further legitimacy to continue the war. Trump has said his administration takes the claim "very seriously."
articles.body: Iran on Tuesday dismissed a CNN report that Tehran was preparing a so-called "dirty bomb plot." US President Donald Trump said his administration was taking the report "very seriously." Tehran's dismissal came after CNN reported on Tuesday that "Iran is developing plans to target senior Trump administration officials by detonating a so-called dirty bomb or a chemical weapon in Washington, DC," citing multiple US intelligence sources. The article also reported that "US intelligence has picked up Iranian chatter claiming that it has stashed bomb-making materials inside the country" and that "many national security officials assume that pre-positioned nuclear materials have already been in the US for years," citing, again, multiple US intelligence sources. To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video When asked about the story during his visit to the Philippines , Trump said that if there was such a threat, Iran would "pay a price the likes of which no other country has ever paid before." "I hope it's not, but we take it very seriously because they happen to be crazy," he added. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei slammed the report, calling it "a malicious campaign to manufacture propaganda." "Those who initiated the aggression against Iran are now seeking to lay the media groundwork for their sinister designs by manufacturing and disseminating baseless allegations," he said on X. "Step by step, they are attempting to manufacture a veneer of legitimacy for further aggression and atrocities," he said, naming CNN's reporting on the alleged "dirty bomb plot" and The New York Times without specifying any of its reporting. Baghaei also said the US and Israel hit water storage reservoirs "during the recent acts of aggression." The Iran war , started by the US and Israeli strikes on February 28, continues as negotiations to bring an end to the fighting stall. Both US and Israel have been holding off from major attacks as they held elections over the last weeks. Tehran has said it is in control the Strait of Hormuz , a key transit point for global oil and natural gas supplies, while continuing to attack ships it considers unauthorized users of the waterway. There are near-daily reports of ships hitting mines in parts of the strait Tehran says are unauthorized for transit. The US Navy, which is enforcing its own blockade of Iranian vessels, has recently escorted tankers through the strait. To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Before the midterm elections, Trump said, "We may do another little Epic Fury," referring to US-Israeli strikes that started the war, though he did not provide any timeframe. Trump is expected to meet Chinese President ‌Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of an APEC leaders' summit in China on Thursday and discuss ending the ​war in Iran. Pakistan-mediated peace talks between the US and Iran on April failed to reach a conclusion. Qatar, another mediator in the war, on Tuesday called for restraint "to avoid any escalation that could undermine negotiation efforts." Iran claims drone attack on US radar system at Sheikh Isa air base in Bahrain
articles.summary: Bahrain was heavily targeted earlier in the war, which started in February, but had been peaceful for weeks until an Iranian drone attack on Friday. A second followed on Sunday.
articles.body: Blasts echoed over the Bahraini capital Manama on Tuesday, as Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they launched a drone attack, the third in five days after a weeks-long lull.Bahrain's armed forces intercepted "Iranian aerial attacks in the kingdom's skies", according to state television, while Iran's Guards said they targeted a US-operated radar system.Bahrain's Interior Ministry, in a post on X, warned of a "possible threat" and called on the country's residents to remain calm, move to the nearest safe place and follow only official sources for information on developments.Bahraini officials also said the country's air defence systems had intercepted attacks from Iran.No confirmed report has yet been released on any impact of Iranian drones on the radar system at Sheikh Isa base or on the extent of any possible damage.The public relations arm of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps described the pre-dawn attack on Tuesday as a response to what it called "the continued violation of the airspace of the Islamic Republic of Iran" by US military drones.It said the operation formed part of ongoing air-defence and electronic warfare measures to track, destroy and capture US drones of the MQ and MQM-170 series."Combat drones belonging to the Revolutionary Guards carried out a precision operation this morning, targeting a radar system operated by US forces at the Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain," the Guards' Sepah news website said.The Guards also warned that continued use of regional bases and military facilities for actions against Iran would not go unanswered.Bahrain was heavily targeted earlier in the war, which started in February, but had been peaceful for weeks until an Iranian drone attack on Friday. A second followed on Sunday.Friday's strike was the first Iranian attack against a Gulf country since early September.The US military said it had shot down two drones launched Friday by Iranian forces, while the Bahraini army said it had intercepted Sunday's attack.Bahrain, which hosts a major US naval base, has experienced numerous Iranian attacks since US-Israeli strikes on Iran triggered the Middle East war in February.Since September, the conflict has mainly been restricted to the area around the strategic Strait of Hormuz, with the US blockading Iranian ports and Tehran attempting to control the oil shipping route.The Middle East war will be on the agenda during an unprecedented trilateral summit between US President Donald Trump and his Chinese and Russian counterparts, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, scheduled this week in China, according to the White House.As talks aimed at ending the war appear to be deadlocked, a third US aircraft carrier, the USS Theodore Roosevelt, is operating in the Middle East, the US military said on Monday.

Serbian Court Seeks Arrest of Kosovo Serb Kingpin Radoicic
articles.summary: Court asks police to issue arrest warrant for businessman and politician after he failed to report to police – violating measures imposed as part of probe into a 2023 shootout in the Kosovo village of Banjska/Banjske.
articles.body: The Higher Court in Belgrade has ordered Milan Radoicic’s detention and that an arrest warrant be issued for him for violating a measure prohibiting him from leaving his place of residence, according to media reports on Tuesday. Radoicic failed to report to Belgrade’s Savski Venac police station on November 15, when he was required to confirm that he was still at his registered place of residence, as ordered by the court. The businessman and former vice-president of the Belgrade-backed Srpska Lista party, who is seen as a ‘kingpin’ operator among Serbs in northern Kosovo, is under investigation over an armed attack on the Kosovo village of Banjska/Banjske in September 2023. The Higher Court in Belgrade confiscated his passport in 2023, and warned that detention may be imposed if he violated the terms imposed on his freedom of movement, which included not leaving his place of residence. He was ordered to appear at a police station twice a month. Belgrade Higher Prosecutor’s Office questioned Radoicic in September 2023 about allegations that he had obtained large amounts of weapons and took them to northern Kosovo, where an armed Serb group was involved in the deadly shootout with Kosovo police in Banjska/Banjske on September 24 that year. Prosecutors allege that Radoicic “procured weapons, ammunition and explosive devices” in Bosnia, “which were delivered to him in the city of Belgrade”. They claim Radoicic “transported and stored [the weapons] in unspecified locations” in Kosovo and “hid them in abandoned buildings and forests”. In the ensuing shootout in Banjska/Banjske, a Kosovo policeman was killed. Three of the gunmen also died. In September 2023, Radoicic said he took sole responsibility for the shootout, while he described as a “defence” operation against the Kosovo authorities, without the knowledge of his political party, Srpska Lista, or the Serbian authorities in Belgrade.

articles.title: 14:42 302 people killed in various incidents in Kyrgyzstan since start of 2026
articles.summary: A total of 3,649 various incidents have been registered in Kyrgyzstan since the beginning of 2026, claiming 302 lives. Minister of Emergency Situations Kanatbek Chynybaev announced this at a meeting of the Zhogorku Kenesh Committee on International Affairs, Defense, Security and Migration.
articles.body: A total of 3,649 various incidents have been registered in Kyrgyzstan since the beginning of 2026, claiming 302 lives. Minister of Emergency Situations Kanatbek Chynybaev announced this at a meeting of the Zhogorku Kenesh Committee on International Affairs, Defense, Security and Migration. According to him, despite a decline in the overall number of incidents compared with last year, the death toll has increased by 24. As of November 15, 2026, material damage caused by the reported incidents amounted to 1,269 billion soms, according to the Ministry of Emergency Situations. For comparison, 3,816 incidents were recorded during the same period in 2025, claiming 278 lives. Material damage amounted to 1,735 billion soms. Thus, the number of incidents decreased by 167, while material damage fell by 466 million soms. The minister also reported that 42 emergencies had been registered in the country since the beginning of this year, claiming 42 lives. The damage amounted to 468,502 million soms. During the same period last year, 14 emergencies were recorded, leaving 32 people dead, while the damage was estimated at 60 million soms. A total of 2,709 fires have been registered in Kyrgyzstan since the beginning of the year, 509 fewer than during the same period in 2025. Material damage caused by fires amounted to 1,213 billion soms, down 518 million soms from last year’s figure. Twenty-two people died in fires, compared with 46 in 2025. Another 30 people were injured, while five were rescued. According to Kanatbek Chynybaev, emergency response teams have rescued 428 people since the beginning of the year. During the same period in 2025, 368 people received assistance.

articles.title: Yerevan suggests car restrictions after Pashinyan’s wife says traffic can cause ‘a heart attack’
articles.summary: Amidst growing criticism over traffic congestion and overcrowded public transport in Yerevan, Mayor Tigran Avinyan has called for possible restrictions on the number of cars and promised to bring proposed measures up for public discussion later in November. The proposal came shortly after Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan’s wife, Anna Hakobyan, said getting around the capital could cause a ‘heart attack’.
articles.body: Amidst growing criticism over traffic congestion and overcrowded public transport in Yerevan, Mayor Tigran Avinyan has called for possible restrictions on the number of cars and promised to bring proposed measures up for public discussion later in November. The proposal came shortly after Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan’s wife, Anna Hakobyan, said getting around the capital could cause a ‘heart attack’. Despite major public transport reforms, including the purchase of new buses and the replacement of minibuses, the city’s transport problems remain unresolved, continuing to fuel public discontent and criticism online over long traffic jams during peak hours, overcrowded transport and bus stops, and public transport delays. Avinyan addressed the issue during a municipal administrative session on Monday, calling it a ‘multilayered’ problem and pointing to major contributing factors, including the growing number of cars and population, along with poor driving habits. In order to address the problem, Avinyan called for restrictions on the number of cars allowed to circulate in the capital, including measures targeting older and highly polluting vehicles. According to him, the number of cars in Yerevan is growing ‘exponentially’, primarily attributing this to Armenia’s economic growth and rising incomes. Over the past 12 years, the number of cars in Armenia had doubled from 500,000 to 1 million, Deputy Mayor Suren Grigoryan said, adding that around 15,000 new cars are registered in Yerevan annually. ‘The first issue we need to discuss is limiting the number of cars circulating in Yerevan. If [critics] tell us that we are once again talking about restrictions, I want to insist that we are already living under restrictions today, because the number of cars has already restricted all of us. Worst of all, it has restricted public transport’, Avinyan said. Avinyan argued that public transport was not underperforming because there were too few buses or trolleybuses, but because of the space taken up by private cars during peak hours, making it difficult for public transport to reach stops, causing even worse traffic jams. He added that public transport should operate ‘like a Swiss watch’, warning that driving in Yerevan would become less convenient in the future as dedicated lanes prioritising public transport are introduced. Avinyan went on to criticise poor driving habits and traffic violations, adding that with the increased number of cars, ‘just 50 cars can bring a city to a standstill’ due to their violations. Among other proposals, he also suggested dividing Yerevan into different zones, introducing dedicated bus lanes, and discussing measures to encourage children to attend schools closer to home. Avinyan stressed the need to create more jobs outside the capital, arguing that the concentration of employment opportunities in Yerevan is contributing to increased traffic. The municipality was instructed on Monday to develop a set of regulations and present the proposed measures for public discussion by the end of next week. The discussion followed criticism from Hakobyan, who recently complained about traffic in Yerevan in a social media video on 10 November. ‘Getting from one place to another in Yerevan is enough for a heart attack’, she said. ‘There are people for whom finding an answer to this question long ago has been part of their job. Although, apparently, it is a somewhat more difficult task than granting construction permits to companies making million-dollar investments’, Hakobyan added, in an apparent reference to the municipality. Avinyan appeared to respond to Hakobyan on Monday by denying that construction growth in the city worsened its traffic. Instead, he said that the growth of Yerevan’s population is not because of construction, but was rather due to the influx of refugees from Nagorno-Karabakh and of foreigners, mainly Russians and Russian—Armenians, due to Russia’s full-scale war against Ukraine. Furthermore, Avinyan defended the continued construction, arguing that slowing the pace of real estate development would have serious consequences for Yerevan’s property and rental markets. He claimed new buildings helped moderate rental prices, which he suggested would otherwise be significantly higher, despite them already being disproportionately high with Yerevan rental pricing and prices of real estate constantly sparking debate online. He also said the municipality had a direct financial interest in construction projects launched since 2022, with fees introduced in 2023 helping fund improvements to hundreds of courtyards, football pitches, roads, and sewage systems. A journalist since 2016, Arshaluys specialises in fact-checking and open-source investigations, with a focus on the Nagorno-Karabakh conflict, politics, and social and gender issues. She is also a strong advocate for media literacy and closely follows Armenia’s media landscape.

articles.title: Armenia infrastructure deputy minister on talks with Russian side: Discussion was on effectiveness of South Caucasus Railway company’s concession agreement
articles.summary: This was our first meeting with our Russian partners, the negotiations were very friendly and quite normal, very much with both feet on the ground, practical, about specific directions, about specific sections. Deputy Minister of Territorial Administration and Infrastructure of Armenia, David Ivanyan, this to RFE/RL on Tuesday after the first meeting of the Armenia-Russia working group on the Armenian railway.
articles.body: This was our first meeting with our Russian partners, the negotiations were very friendly and quite normal, very much with both feet on the ground, practical, about specific directions, about specific sections. Deputy Minister of Territorial Administration and Infrastructure of Armenia, David Ivanyan, this to RFE/RL on Tuesday after the first meeting of the Armenia-Russia working group on the Armenian railway. “The main topics on the agenda were the matters set by the [Armenian] prime minister about the effectiveness of our concession [agreement with the South Caucasus Railway company], and of course about the directions that we want to develop,” Ivanyan said, and added that one of the topics discussed was the restoration of Armenia’s railway sections. When asked whether the Russian side is inclined to participate in these activities, the deputy minister replied: “Look, this is the first meeting. Of course, we will still touch on many technical details, but in general, a normal, appropriate discussion is taking place. The discussion was on the matters set by the [Armenian] prime minister. At the moment, there was a discussion about the effectiveness of the concession and its further development.” As for what arguments the Russian side brings, claiming whether the Russian concession management of the Armenian railway is effective, Ivanyan replied: “We have not yet reached that stage to be able to answer that question. This was our first meeting, that’s why I will inform the details additionally.” Earlier, Armenian News-NEWS.am reported that the first meeting of the Armenian-Russian working group to discuss the matters of the Armenian railway, which is under the concession management of South Caucasus Railway, a subsidiary of Russian Railways, had kicked off in Yerevan. The meeting was being held in a closed format, without the participation of the media, and an official statement on it will be issued later, had informed the Ministry of Territorial Administration and Infrastructure of Armenia. The aforesaid Armenian-Russian working group was set up in October for a three-month period, the purpose of which is to find solutions to matters related to the operation of the Armenian railway. The matter arose earlier this year, when Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan stated that the management of Armenian railway by the aforementioned Russian company “deprives Armenia of strategic positions and competitive advantages.” Later, Pashinyan suggested that Moscow consider the possibility of transferring its concession management of the Armenian railway to a friendly third country, and noted Kazakhstan, in particular, among the potential options.

articles.title: FMs of Uzbekistan, Oman and Iran Hold Talks in Muscat
articles.summary: The foreign ministers of Uzbekistan, Oman and Iran discussed trade, transport links and regional tensions at a trilateral meeting in Muscat.
articles.body: Tashkent, Uzbekistan (UzDaily.uz) — The foreign ministers of Uzbekistan, Oman and Iran held a trilateral meeting in Muscat to discuss economic cooperation and the regional situation, Uzbekistan's Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov said. The talks were attended by Oman's Foreign Minister Sayyid Badr bin Hamad al-Busaidi and Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi. The ministers discussed prospects for expanding trade and economic ties between their countries. They also focused on developing transport and logistics cooperation and making more effective use of existing transit potential. The participants exchanged views on the regional situation. They stressed the need to resolve ongoing tensions through diplomatic means and continue dialogue between the parties. The ministers also highlighted the importance of expanding practical cooperation and making use of existing opportunities for joint work. The sides expressed their readiness to continue coordinated efforts to promote peace, stability and development in the region.

articles.title: Constitutional Court rejects UNM motion seeking clarification of legal standards in party ban case
articles.summary: The Plenum of Georgia’s Constitutional Court has rejected a motion filed by United National Movement (UNM) representative Zaza Bibilashvili, ruling that procedural decisions already adopted by the Court are not subject to review.
articles.body: The Plenum of Georgia’s Constitutional Court has rejected a motion filed by United National Movement (UNM) representative Zaza Bibilashvili, ruling that procedural decisions already adopted by the Court are not subject to review. The motion, submitted during ongoing hearings concerning a lawsuit seeking to ban opposition political parties, called on the Court to clarify the legal standards applicable to the proceedings before issuing its final judgment. Bibilashvili requested that the Court issue an interim ruling or written clarification addressing three key issues: the specific matters requiring proof under Article 23 of the Georgian Constitution for each defendant; the allocation of the burden of proof, taking into account the presumption of constitutionality of political parties’ activities; and the standards of proof and evaluation of evidence. He argued that establishing these standards in advance was essential to ensuring that the defendants could effectively exercise their right to defense. “We are dealing with a case of such magnitude, as citizens of this country, that I do not understand how 20 or 30 minutes, or even a day, could compare with the potentially catastrophic consequences this case may have,” Bibilashvili said. He warned that the consequences could extend beyond the prohibition of political parties, suggesting that Russia could use the proceedings to justify its own actions. Bibilashvili claimed that the Court faced a choice between clarifying the applicable legal standards before the remaining procedural stages or establishing them only in its final judgment, when the parties would no longer have an opportunity to adjust their defense accordingly. Responding to the motion, Georgian Dream representative Archil Gorduladze accused Bibilashvili of using the courtroom for political statements rather than addressing legal issues. Gorduladze argued that the opposition was attempting to revisit procedural matters already considered by the Court and questioned why the defendants continued to seek clarification of the allegations against them. “Make up your minds about whether this lawsuit contains evidence. Make up your minds about whether you have answers to the numerous allegations we have presented concerning systemic crimes,” Gorduladze said. He also referred to an earlier motion by Coalition for Change representative Nika Gvaramia, who had requested advance clarification of when a potential decision banning political parties would take effect. Gorduladze argued that both motions sought to have the Court determine aspects of its eventual ruling before completing its examination of the case. Following consideration of the arguments, the Constitutional Court's Plenum rejected Bibilashvili’s motion. Announcing the decision, Judge Revaz Nadaraia explained that the motion effectively challenged procedural rulings previously issued by the Plenum in response to requests from the parties. “Rulings adopted by the Court's Plenum are not subject to review,” Nadaraia stated. He also rejected the request for advance clarification of evidentiary standards, arguing that it would effectively require the Court to indicate beforehand which evidence it intended to use and for what purpose. “This is inconceivable,” Nadaraia said. The proceedings concern a constitutional lawsuit initiated by Georgian Dream seeking the prohibition of opposition political parties. The case remains under consideration by the Constitutional Court.

articles.title: The Constitutional Court plenum did not satisfy the motion of the "National Movement" representative, stating that rulings already adopted are not subject to revision
articles.summary: "Let's figure it out—does this lawsuit have evidence or not? Figure out the charges presented by us, which are numerous regarding systemic crimes, and whether you have answers," Archil Gorduladze, the representative of "Georgian Dream" in the Constitutional Court, stated in response to the motion by Zaza Bibilashvili, the representative of the "National Movement."
articles.body: "Let's figure it out—does this lawsuit have evidence or not? Figure out the charges presented by us, which are numerous regarding systemic crimes, and whether you have answers," Archil Gorduladze, the representative of "Georgian Dream" in the Constitutional Court, stated in response to the motion by Zaza Bibilashvili, the representative of the "National Movement." Zaza Bibilashvili's motion included 3 aspects, and its primary demand in relation to this specific case was for the court to define specific standards. "Let the Constitutional Court adopt a ruling or issue a written explanation before resolving the case on its merits, which defines in the case of banning political parties: 1. The subject of proof in relation to each precondition provided for by Article 23 of the Constitution of Georgia for each respondent. 2. The rule of distribution of the burden of proof, taking into account the presumption of constitutionality of political activities' of political parties. 3. The standard of proof and standards for evaluating evidence — this is our motion, and I repeat once again, we are tackling such a massive case as citizens of this country that I do not know how 20-30 minutes, or even a day, could be connected to the possible catastrophic consequences that might follow this case, not only through the banning of parties, but also through what Russia will 'whitewash' with this lawsuit. The court faces the following choice: to define the standards now and thereby give the parties the opportunity to fully defend their interests and consequently the interests of the country, or later, post-factum, tell us in an already adopted decision what we could and should have known now. Especially under conditions when your ruling has established that these standards do not exist and need to be determined. Let those standards be established through an interim decision or explanation, with which we must defend ourselves in the remaining procedural stages now," Bibilashvili stated. The plaintiff's side responded to this motion by the "National Movement," explaining that Zaza Bibilashvili was using the high tribune to make political statements, that his motion strayed from legal issues, and that he spoke incorrectly about facts. "Mr. Zaza Bibilashvili used the tribune to do everything that had already been said during the explanations—the purpose of this is also interesting. It strays entirely from legal issues, and he also made statements on political issues. He addressed us, and as for facts, he spoke about them entirely incorrectly. Do you know what the main thing is? 'Zaza, come back immediately and show class, remind them that a successful state was created under the hands of numerous betrayals by a group of successful politicians' — these are the words of Mikheil Saakashvili . Over three days of answering judges' questions, quoting a judge from European Court of Human Rights decisions, and answering questions in a way that wasn't what they might have given, they filed a motion for the judge's recusal so that such questions would no longer be asked. Despite the fact that more than one lie was voiced specifically by representatives of the 'National Movement' and that these lies deserve an appropriate assessment by society, Mr. Zaza now used this tribune to make a political speech, including telling an absolute lie regarding the 30th anniversary of the court. Turns out, how dare the Chairman of Parliament attend a specific event? Mr. Zaza, I know about your qualifications and I am sure you well know that in the case of norm-control, in the absolute majority of cases, the Parliament of Georgia is the respondent, and what are we to do? Because it is the respondent and the Chairman of Parliament signs the mandate regarding specific representatives, does that mean he should not attend any event of the Constitutional Court? What is the 'National Movement' asking for? If, for example, for 'New Changes,' Mr. Gramamia was demanding just a few days ago that one of the components of the decision—that is, when it should enter into force—be announced in advance and a decision be adopted, now Mr. Zaza Bibilashvili is demanding that the plenum deliberate in advance and establish what standards should be used and how specific facts should be evaluated. Let's figure it out—does this lawsuit have evidence or not? Figure out the charges presented by us, which are numerous regarding systemic crimes, and whether you have answers, and stop returning to where we were 13 days ago. It's the 14th day, and 13 days ago you were saying 'we don't know who is challenging us,' and today you come out when the judges have almost finished answering the parties and you are still saying 'we don't know who is challenging us.' You simply cannot do this, and I ask you, Mr. Judge, to ensure that the high tribune is not used to make political statements and to return to the stage that a specific party has already passed," Gorduladze stated. The judges' plenum did not satisfy the motion of "National Movement" representative Zaza Bibilashvili and stated that "rulings adopted by the court plenum are not subject to revision." "The motion should not be satisfied and is not satisfied due to the following circumstances: the party is practically appealing, and with the content of its motion, it dislikes the rulings that were issued by the plenum during the case review stage in response to the parties' motion. Rulings adopted by the court plenum are not subject to revision. As for the standard of evidence, it is read in a certain way that the party wants the court to tell it in advance what evidence it will use for what and for what purpose. This is unbelievable," Revaz Nadaraia stated.

articles.title: Buchukuri: ‘The issues being examined by the Constitutional Court are irrelevant’
articles.summary: Ana Buchukuri, one of the leaders of the Gakharia for Georgia party, has questioned the relevance of the issues being examined by the Constitutional Court in proceedings concerning a lawsuit seeking to ban several opposition parties. “It is the 14th day of hearings, and today it should be our turn to be questioned.
articles.body: Ana Buchukuri, one of the leaders of the Gakharia for Georgia party, has questioned the relevance of the issues being examined by the Constitutional Court in proceedings concerning a lawsuit seeking to ban several opposition parties. “It is the 14th day of hearings, and today it should be our turn to be questioned. To be honest, the issues the court is examining are so irrelevant that there is no constitutional basis for them. None of the questions raised by the judges yesterday concerned our party, because we have always held a different position, from vetting to our non-participation in the alliance,” Buchukuri told journalists at the Constitutional Court. She said she was interested in what questions the judges would put to her party, adding that the proceedings did not constitute a genuine legal process. “Ultimately, you know that what is currently taking place at the Constitutional Court is not a legal process. Unfortunately, the parties present here, including the respondent side, cannot influence the decision. Society can see the difference in terms of competence. People can sense it. They may not follow specific legal terms and arguments, but they naturally recognize it,” she said. The Constitutional Court is hearing a lawsuit filed by Georgian Dream seeking to ban three opposition political groups: the United National Movement, the Coalition for Change and Strong Georgia. The ruling party accuses them of violating constitutional principles and seeks to have their activities prohibited. Related Story: Opposition Ban Case Deepens as Court Hearings Become Increasingly Contentious

articles.title: US addresses rumors of a Nov. 17 blackout
articles.summary: The U.S. Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) stated on X that social media reports of power and internet outages and disruptions in banking operations are not true. What is actually happening on Nov. 17?
articles.body: The U.S. Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) stated on X that social media reports of power and internet outages and disruptions in banking operations are not true. FEMA and the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) will jointly conduct a nationwide test of the Emergency Alert System (EAS). The test is scheduled to begin at 2:20 p.m. ET and last approximately one minute. Regular TV and radio broadcasts will be interrupted by a test message in English and Spanish. «It lasts 1 minute, and no action is required. No blackouts, no secret emergencies. Just our legally mandated, routine test on TV and radio at approximately 2:20 PM ET,» the agency said in a post on X. FEMA stressed that the test is unrelated to any emergency and does not involve outages affecting electricity, communications, internet or banking services. Claims of a digital catastrophe allegedly set to strike on Nov. 17, 2026, has been widely circulating on social media. The authors of the posts claim that hackers will breach banks worldwide, wipe out bank account balances and shut down the internet for three months. Media reports say that on Oct. 31, a user going by the nickname Wesley posted about an impending collapse. He claimed that an acquaintance with ties to the darknet had warned him about it. The author provided no verifiable evidence. Initially, the post mentioned a mysterious «COVID 2.0.» Details about bank breaches, wiped-out account balances and a prolonged internet shutdown emerged as the story spread further. Furthermore, social media users began referencing an episode of «The Simpsons,» titled «It’s a Blunderful Life» (Season 35, 2023), in which a power outage hits the fictional town of Springfield on Nov. 17. However, the animated series makes no mention of either 2026 or global cyberattacks. Kursiv.media previously reported that several major U.S. banks experienced widespread disruptions to their online services on Nov. 16. In a separate report, Kursiv.media examined rumors of a «digital apocalypse» allegedly scheduled for Nov. 17. Kazakhstanis were warned of mass cyberattacks, wiped-out bank account balances and a three-month internet shutdown. However, the country’s Ministry of Emergency Situations dismissed these reports.

articles.title: 11:50 Lawmakers approve Almazbek Moldobaev for judge of Constitutional Court
articles.summary: The Zhogorku Kenesh Committee on Constitutional Legislation approved the nomination of Almazbek Moldobaev for the position of judge of the Constitutional Court of Kyrgyzstan. His candidacy was submitted for parliamentary consideration by President Sadyr Japarov.
articles.body: The Zhogorku Kenesh Committee on Constitutional Legislation approved the nomination of Almazbek Moldobaev for the position of judge of the Constitutional Court of Kyrgyzstan. His candidacy was submitted for parliamentary consideration by President Sadyr Japarov. Almazbek Moldobaev currently serves as the Permanent Representative of the President and the Cabinet of Ministers to the Constitutional Court. Born on February 9, 1973, in Frunze, Almazbek Moldobaev graduated from the Faculty of Law at the Zhusup Balasagyn Kyrgyz National University in 1995. He later pursued further education at the Military-Diplomatic Academy and completed postgraduate studies at the Military University of the Ministry of Defense of the Russian Federation. From 2006 to 2015, he served as a judge at the Pervomaisky District Court in Bishkek. Over the years, he has also held various positions within the Office of the President and the Zhogorku Kenesh. From 2019 to 2023, he headed a department within the Zhogorku Kenesh Committee on Law and Order, Combating Crime, and Countering Corruption. He holds the academic degree of Candidate of Legal Sciences, the civil service rank of 1st-class State Civil Service Counselor, and the military rank of Colonel of Justice.

articles.title: Moldova to participate in Ukraine’s demining efforts after war ends
articles.summary: Deputy Prime Minister, Minister of Foreign Affairs Mihai Popșoi participated in the fourth edition of Ukraine Mine Action Conference, held in Brussels. The official reaffirmed the Republic of Moldova’s commitment to contributing to humanitarian demining efforts in Ukraine once a ceasefire is established.
articles.body: Deputy Prime Minister, Minister of Foreign Affairs Mihai Popșoi participated in the fourth edition of Ukraine Mine Action Conference, held in Brussels. The official reaffirmed the Republic of Moldova’s commitment to contributing to humanitarian demining efforts in Ukraine once a ceasefire is established. UMAC 2026: Clearing the way in partnership - organized by the European Union and Ukraine in partnership with Belgium, and brought together officials, representatives of international organizations, academia and private sector, as well as operators involved in mine action. In his address, Mihai Popșoi emphasized the need to maintain international support for Ukraine and coordinate efforts to reduce the risks posed by landmines and explosive remnants of war. The minister pointed out that these munitions pose a danger to the population even after the war ends, while the effects of Russian aggression extend beyond Ukraine’s borders. The head of Moldova’s diplomacy highlighted the support provided by the Republic of Moldova by facilitating the training of Ukrainian personnel for humanitarian mine action. He also reiterated the country’s readiness to participate in demining efforts in Ukraine once a ceasefire is established. The Republic of Moldova also joined the Joint Declaration adopted during the conference. Through the document, participants pledge to coordinate their efforts to accelerate the recovery and reconstruction of mine-affected areas, strengthen international demining activities and ensure safer conditions for affected communities. At the end of his address, Mihai Popșoi reiterated the Republic of Moldova’s support for Ukraine and for international efforts to achieve lasting peace. 7 drones cross into Moldovan airspace during latest Russian attack against Ukraine, 1 spotted over Chisinau
articles.summary: Seven drones crossed into Moldovan airspace during the latest Russian mass attack against Ukraine, with one Shahed-type drone spotted flying over Chisinau on Nov. 17, the Moldovan Defense Ministry reported. Five of the drones crashed near the villages of Cheltuitori, Pohorniceni, Pohrebeni, Cuhurestii de Jos and Baxani, according to the Moldovan Defense Ministry.
articles.body: Seven drones crossed into Moldovan airspace during the latest Russian mass attack against Ukraine, with one Shahed-type drone spotted flying over Chisinau on Nov. 17, the Moldovan Defense Ministry reported. Five of the drones crashed near the villages of Cheltuitori, Pohorniceni, Pohrebeni, Cuhurestii de Jos and Baxani, according to the Moldovan Defense Ministry. A possible sixth impact has been reported in the Ocnita district, while the seventh drone disappeared from monitoring systems near the town of Leova. There have been no reported casualties. Not all of the settlements are located along Moldova's border with Ukraine. The village of Cheltuitori is some 10.7 kilometers (6.6 miles) from Chisinau. Moldova's President Maia Sandu condemned the latest in a series of Russian incursions into the country's airspace, saying that Moldovans are worried because it shows Moscow "cares neither about neutrality, nor sovereignty, nor human life." "Moldova wants peace. Moldova is working for peace. We still do not have the necessary defense capabilities to protect ourselves from drones that threaten our security," Sandu added. "That is precisely why we will continue to condemn this inhumane war and demand sanctions against Russia until it is forced to stop it." Russian drone incursions into Moldovan airspace have become more and more frequent. Moldova declared a member of the Russian embassy in Moldova persona non grata on Oct. 23 after a Russian drone violated Moldova's air space and fell near homes in one of the country's central regions. Moldovan police found drone fragments in an area bordering Ukraine's southern Odesa Oblast on Nov. 12.

articles.title: Armenian, Russian Officials Open Railway Talks
articles.summary: Speaking after the meeting held in Yerevan on Tuesday, Deputy Minister of Territorial Administration and Infrastructure Davit Ivanian described the discussions as constructive and practical, noting that the two sides focused on specific railway directions and sections. “The talks took place in a very friendly, fairly normal, down-to-earth and businesslike atmosphere regarding concrete directions and sections,” Ivanian said.
articles.body: Speaking after the meeting held in Yerevan on Tuesday, Deputy Minister of Territorial Administration and Infrastructure Davit Ivanian described the discussions as constructive and practical, noting that the two sides focused on specific railway directions and sections. “The talks took place in a very friendly, fairly normal, down-to-earth and businesslike atmosphere regarding concrete directions and sections,” Ivanian said. When asked whether the Russian side had substantiated the efficiency of its management of the railway system, Ivanian said the discussions had not yet reached that stage. “We have not yet come to that stage to be able to answer that question,” he said. The joint Armenian-Russian working group was established in October for a three-month term to address issues related to the operation of Armenia’s railways, which have been managed since 2008 by South Caucasus Railway, a wholly owned subsidiary of the state-run Russian Railways company. According to Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinian, the group is mandated to submit proposals aimed at increasing the competitiveness of the Armenian railway network. Ivanian, who leads the Armenian delegation, said further steps will be determined based on the conclusions reached at the end of the three-month discussion format. The Russian side in the working group is represented by Deputy Transport Minister Aleksei Shilo and Russian Railways Deputy CEO Vyacheslav Pavlovsky. According to Ivanian, during the opening session, the sides also addressed proposals to restore two currently non-operational cross-border railway sections: one running from the Armenian village of Yeraskh to the border with Azerbaijan’s Nakhichevan exclave, and another from the Armenian town of Gyumri to the Turkish border. Ivanian noted that because it was the group’s first meeting, many technical details remain to be addressed in future sessions. “But it was a very normal, to-the-point discussion,” he added. In early October, Moscow stated that it was awaiting Yerevan’s response to a Russian proposal regarding the restoration of those two border sections. The establishment of the working group followed months of friction over the future of the concession. Earlier this year, Yerevan proposed that Moscow transfer the management of Armenia’s railway network to a third country acceptable to both Armenia and Russia. Moscow rejected the proposal, warning that any unilateral alteration of the concession terms or termination of the contract could prompt Russia to demand the return of roughly $400 million in investments made in the network. Tensions eased in October when Russian Railways CEO Oleg Belozyorov visited Yerevan and met with Pashinian. Following those talks, both sides announced their intention to continue joint work. Under the 30-year concession agreement signed in 2008, Russian Railways is entitled to manage Armenia’s rail infrastructure through its local subsidiary until 2038. To trigger an optional 10-year extension of the deal, the two sides must submit formal proposals to each other by August 2027.

Prison Release Plea for Besieger of Sarajevo Rejected Yet Again
articles.summary: The UN court has denied wartime Bosnian Serb Army officer Dragomir Milosevic’s early release request for a fourth time, citing a lack of ‘sufficient signs’ of rehabilitation.
articles.body: This post is also available in this language: Shqip Bos/Hrv/Srp Dragomir Milosevic in court in The Hague, December 2004 . Photo: EPA/JUAN VRIJDAG. The UN’s International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals in The Hague announced on Tuesday that it has rejected a request for the early release of Dragomir Milosevic, the wartime commander of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps of the Bosnian Serb Army, who was sentenced to 29 years in prison for crimes against civilians in besieged Sarajevo. The president of the International Residual Mechanism, Judge Graciela Gatti Santana, stated in her decision that although Milosevic meets the eligibility requirements for consideration for early release, she believes that the request should be denied. “The high gravity of his crimes strongly militates against granting him early release and Milosevic has not demonstrated sufficient signs of rehabilitation. Further, there is no evidence before me that establishes the existence of compelling humanitarian grounds which would warrant overriding this negative assessment,” Gatti Santana explained. The decision states that Milosevic, who is now 84, clearly suffers from several chronic health conditions. It also states that his behaviour in prison has been consistently good. “However, I have no information that would suggest that Milosevic has engaged in any further reflection about his crimes and specific role in them, or any other positive conduct that could demonstrate a level of rehabilitation that would warrant the exceptional relief of early release,” Gatti Santana said. Milosevic was convicted of bearing responsibility for terrorising civilians in besieged Sarajevo with a campaign of sniper and artillery attacks as commander of the Bosnian Serb Army’s Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. The Hague Tribunal also convicted the wartime Bosnian Serb political and military leaders, Radovan Karadzic and Ratko Mladic, and another former commander of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, Stanislav Galic, of similar offences. During the 44-month siege of Sarajevo by Bosnian Serb forces, more than 11,000 residents of Sarajevo were killed, including around 1,600 children.

articles.title: HOWO and Volvo trucks to be manufactured in Kazakhstan, talks with Mercedes underway
articles.summary: Construction of the Saran Machinery plant in Saran, Karaganda region, which will manufacture Chinese HOWO and Sinotruk trucks, is nearing completion. Meanwhile, Volvo trucks are set to be manufactured in Almaty, with negotiations underway over the potential manufacturing of Mercedes-Benz trucks.
articles.body: Construction of the Saran Machinery plant in Saran, Karaganda region, which will manufacture Chinese HOWO and Sinotruk trucks, is nearing completion. Meanwhile, Volvo trucks are set to be manufactured in Almaty, with negotiations underway over the potential manufacturing of Mercedes-Benz trucks. During a government meeting, Kazakhstan’s Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov said the country would localize production of heavy-duty trucks made by international brands to develop its logistics potential and modernize its vehicle fleet. «Manufacturing of HOWO, Sinotruk and Scania trucks has already been established. Work is underway to increase the local content of their components. In addition, manufacturing of Volvo trucks is planned to begin in Almaty by the end of this year, while negotiations with Mercedes are ongoing,» Bektenov said. Notably, Volvo FH13 trucks will be manufactured in Kazakhstan at the Astana Motors plant. The agreement was signed in June. Industry and Construction Minister Yersaiyn Nagaspayev presented the Saran Machinery plant project as one of the key industrial projects scheduled for implementation in 2026. The facility is expected to manufacture up to 10,000 HOWO trucks annually. The project is valued at 24 billion tenge (approximately $53.9 million). At the initial stage, only truck cabs and chassis will be manufactured, with welding and painting lines scheduled to become operational later in 2026. In the longer term, the plant is expected to transition to full-cycle production using domestically produced components. The project is being implemented jointly with Chinese truck manufacturer Sinotruk. The Kazakhstani partner is MashZavod (Saran Machine-Building Plant), controlled by Timur Karbayev . Nagaspayev also named several other key industrial investment projects planned for 2026. One of them is the VOLTREX motor oil plant, currently under construction in Shymkent, with an estimated project cost of 48 billion tenge (approximately $107.9 million). The facility is designed to manufacture 50,000 units annually. The company’s founder is Yerkebulan Ilyassov , son of Saidulla Kozhabayev , the majority shareholder and founder of Alageum Group. Kozhabayev ranks 47th on Forbes’ list of Kazakhstan’s richest people, with an estimated net worth of $215 million. The third project involves the manufacture of pipes and pipe fittings by QazExpo Centre-Pipe, with an estimated investment of 26.8 billion tenge ($60.2 million). The facility is designed to produce 20,000 units annually. The company already operates a pipe manufacturing facility in Uralsk. It is owned by Lazat Yessekeyeva and Sergey Martsev .

articles.summary: The dissatisfaction voiced in the ongoing protests with the long dominance of the Socialists and Democrats is rattling both camps ahead of 2027’s local elections – but can a new political force emerge to challenge them?
articles.body: The two camps of Albania’s traditional political establishment, the Socialists and the Democrats, are revving up their campaign engines ahead of the May 2027 local elections. Meanwhile, at the Albania-Finland football match at Air Albania Stadium on the evening of November 12, fans were also making their voices on the political situation heard. Albanian team supporters took over the post-victory celebrations with chants of “Rama, resign!” and “Rama, go!”, references to Socialist Prime Minister Edi Rama. A large banner featuring an image of a bloodshot eye was also unfurled in the stands – a tribute to 28-year-old Erjon Vishkuli, who was hit in the eye by a rubber bullet during the ongoing anti-government protests in Tirana. Vance vows US won’t make long-term commitment to Iran war
articles.summary: Vice President Vance on Monday vowed that the U.S. will not make a long-term commitment to the Iran war compared with past U.S. wars in the Middle East. Fox News host Laura Ingraham told Vance that he was being blamed for the memorandum of understanding between the U.S. and Iran not being a success for…
articles.body: Vice President Vance on Monday vowed that the U.S. will not make a long-term commitment to the Iran war compared with past U.S. wars in the Middle East. Fox News host Laura Ingraham told Vance that he was being blamed for the memorandum of understanding between the U.S. and Iran not being a success for Republicans before the 2026 midterm elections. Vance defended President Trump and said the president still has "a lot of options." "He ultimately decides to bring the conflict to a close," Vance said. "He is not going to let this become a forever war, and the people who want it to become a forever war, they can attack me all they want to, because we signed up to not do this." The vice president elaborated that Trump campaigned on not starting new conflicts across the globe, though Trump later suggested the opposite. Trump decided to strike Iran because "he felt he had to destroy the nuclear program," Vance said. "But we are not going to allow this to become a 10- to 15-year commitment or, frankly, even a two-year commitment, despite the fact that a lot of neoconservatives and a lot of other people want us to stay there forever," he said. "We're not going to stay there forever." The vice president said he has "full confidence" Trump will resolve the conflict "with great results for the American people." The conflict was at a standstill for two months following multiple attempts to reach a ceasefire agreement. This was until three recent attacks launched by the Islamic regime. The third of these attacks was on Tuesday, when Iran fired multiple one-way attack drones towards a U.S. radar facility in Bahrain. The drones were intercepted with no damage or injury to U.S. service members, according to U.S. Central Command. Trump has signaled that he would not escalate the conflict after recent negotiations helped lower the steep price of gas, declaring the conflict "effectively over." He dismissed reports that Iran is developing plans to deploy a "dirty bomb" on Washington. "Well if there is, they will pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before," Trump told reporters in Manila, Philippines, when asked about the plot. Qatar led the push earlier this month for both sides to return to the negotiating table, with the backing of Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey. These talks appeared to have since stalled. Iran has offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which it effectively closed off since the start of the conflict, as one of several conditions to end the conflict. Tehran has also requested that U.S. sanctions be lifted and that frozen assets be released, but the administration has rejected these conditions.
